## PACKING TIMELINE & ROOM-BY-ROOM CHECKLIST

### Cross-Country Declutter Rules
Movers charge by weight/volume, and trucks charge by size. Ask yourself: *"Would I pay $10–$20 to ship this item to Oregon?"*
*   **Dump the heavy/cheap stuff:** Particle-board furniture (IKEA), old textbooks, half-empty cleaning bottles, expired pantry goods, and cheap cookware rarely survive or justify the cost of a 2,400-mile trip.
*   **Ohio vs. Oregon Climate Check:** Keep your rain gear and layering fleece! However, if you're moving to the Willamette Valley (Portland/Eugene/Salem), you won't need heavy-duty Midwest snow blowers, 40-lb bags of rock salt, or extreme sub-zero parkas. Sell them in Ohio where they have value.

### Room-by-Room Packing Order (Weeks 6 down to Week 1)

**1. Garage, Storage & Shed (Start Weeks 6–5)** — *Resp: **J** | Est. Time: 4–6 hrs*
*   [ ] **Declutter:** Hazmat items (movers **will not** take paint, propane, bleach, aerosols, motor oil, or fertilizer). Give to neighbors or take to an Ohio hazmat drop-off.
*   [ ] **Pack:** Camping gear, seasonal holiday decor, hand tools (keep a basic toolkit out for furniture disassembly).
*   [ ] **Prep:** Drain fuel and oil from any gas-powered lawn equipment completely.

**2. Guest Room, Office & Decor (Weeks 4–3)** — *Resp: **P** | Est. Time: 3–5 hrs*
*   [ ] **Declutter:** Shred old bills/paperwork; donate books you won't reread; recycle mystery cables.
*   [ ] **Pack:** Artwork (use mirror boxes), books (use **small** boxes only so bottoms don’t blow out), spare linens, out-of-season clothes.
*   [ ] **Tech:** Back up computers to the cloud/external drive. Take a photo of the back of your TV/monitor setup before unplugging cords. Pack electronics in original boxes or heavily padded medium boxes.

**3. Living Room (Week 3–2)** — *Resp: **J** | Est. Time: 3–4 hrs*
*   [ ] **Pack:** Board games, decorative pillows, rugs (rolled and taped), lamps (remove bulbs and pack shades separately in lightweight boxes).
*   [ ] **Furniture:** Put all screws, bolts, and Allen wrenches from disassembled furniture into labeled Ziploc bags, and **tape them securely to the underside** of the furniture piece.

**4. Bedrooms & Closets (Week 2)** — *Resp: **M & P (own clothes)** | Est. Time: 3–4 hrs*
*   [ ] **Declutter:** Anything not worn in 12 months.
*   [ ] **Pack:** Use wardrobe boxes for hanging clothes (fast and keeps them unwrinkled) or leave clothes on hangers and pull heavy-duty drawstring trash bags up from the bottom, tying at the hooks.
*   [ ] **Valuables:** Pack jewelry, heirlooms, and watches into your personal car luggage—never on the moving truck.

**5. Kitchen & Dining (Week 1 — Biggest Boss Battle)** — *Resp: **J** | Est. Time: 6–8 hrs*
*   [ ] **Declutter:** Toss expired spices, chipped mugs, mismatched Tupperware, and heavy canned goods (donate to food bank).
*   [ ] **Pack:** Wrap dishes individually in packing paper; **stack plates vertically on their edges** (like records), not flat, to prevent road-vibration shattering. Use cell dividers for glasses/stemware.
*   [ ] **Appliances:** Tape stove knobs, toaster trays, and microwave glass turntables separately.
*   [ ] **Leave Out:** 1 skillet, 1 pot, 2 plates/bowls/forks/mugs (or switch to paper plates for the final 3 days).

**6. Bathrooms (Days 3–2 before move)** — *Resp: **M** | Est. Time: 1–2 hrs*
*   [ ] **Declutter:** Toss old medications, nearly empty shampoos, and rusty razors.
*   [ ] **Pack:** Place liquid toiletries inside Ziploc bags (changes in elevation over the Rockies *will* make bottles leak). Pack towels last—they make great box gap-fillers.

## DOG-SPECIFIC MASTER CHECKLIST

*Responsibility: Mostly **M** (with **J** on travel days) | Total Prep Time: ~4–5 hrs*

**Vet & Legal Prep (Weeks 6–2)**
*   [ ] **Certificate of Veterinary Inspection (CVI):** Oregon requires a health certificate issued within 30 days of entry for dogs entering the state (rarely checked at highway borders, but required by law and needed by some hotels/boarders).
*   [ ] **Vaccines:** Get a printed copy of the Rabies certificate and DHPP/Bordetella records. (Note: Heartworm is less prevalent in parts of OR than OH, while flea/tick seasons differ, and **Leptospirosis** is a big deal in wet PNW climates—ask your vet about the Lepto vaccine before leaving!)
*   [ ] **Meds:** Get a 60-day supply of all regular preventatives, plus a mild sedative (like Trazodone or Gabapentin) or anti-nausea med (Cerenia) if your dog struggles with 8+ hour car days. **Test the sedative at home 1 week before the trip** to ensure no weird reactions.
*   [ ] **ID:** Put a temporary tag on the collar with both of your cell numbers.

**Road Trip Comfort & Safety**
*   [ ] **Restraint:** Set up a crash-tested harness clip, hammock seat cover, or secured crate in the back seat (ensure AC vents can reach them unhindered by luggage).
*   [ ] **Water Consistency:** Bring 2–3 gallons of Ohio tap water (or bottled water) to mix gradually with new water along the route—sudden water changes frequently give dogs diarrhea on road trips.
*   [ ] **PNW Hazard Prep:** If driving through eastern Oregon/Idaho in summer/early fall, watch out for **cheatgrass/foxtails** at highway rest stops (they burrow into paws/ears/noses). Stick to paved or mowed areas.

**Overnight Hotel Strategy**
*   [ ] **Booking:** Use filters on BringFido.com or book consistently dog-friendly chains (*La Quinta, Kimpton, Home2 Suites, Residence Inn, Best Western*). Always check weight limits and fee policies ($0–$75/night).
*   [ ] **Room Choice:** Request a **first-floor room near a side exit** when checking in—it makes midnight potty runs infinitely easier.
*   [ ] **Settling In:** Bring an unwashed blanket or t-shirt that smells like home/you. Turn on the hotel room bathroom fan or a white-noise phone app at night so hallway footsteps don't trigger barking in a strange place.

## SERVICES & SUBSCRIPTIONS TIMELINE

*Responsibility: **P** (Financial/Digital) & **M** (Home Services) | Est. Time: 2–3 hrs total*

*   **4 Weeks Out (Cancel Local):** Gym memberships (often require 30-day in-person or certified mail notice), local CSA/farm boxes, lawn care, pest control, house cleaners, local museum/zoo passes.
*   **2 Weeks Out (Transfer/Shutdown Utilities):**
    *   *Ohio Shutoffs (set for Day AFTER Move-Out):* Electric, gas, water/sewer, trash, internet/cable (schedule equipment return to UPS store—**keep the receipt!**).
    *   *Oregon Starts (set for Day BEFORE Arrival):* Electric (e.g., PGE, Pacific Power), gas (NW Natural), water, municipal trash/recycling/compost, internet.
*   **1 Week Out (Address Updates):**
    *   **Financial:** Banks, credit cards, Venmo/PayPal, investment accounts, auto-loan lenders (crucial so your billing zip code matches at gas pumps on the road!).
    *   **Shopping/Shipping:** Amazon (delete your old default address immediately after the move so you don’t accidentally prime-ship to Ohio!), Chewy (dog food auto-ship), meal kits, prescription delivery.
    *   **Official:** Employer HR/Payroll (ensure state tax withholding switches from OH + Ohio municipal RITA/CCA taxes to OR state tax on your move date), IRS Form 8822, auto & renters/homeowners insurance.
